hetsiren.name: hetsiren
hetsiren.description: Heterogeneous volume reconstruction with HetSIREN neural network

fields.name: md
fields.help: Xmipp/Relion metadata file with the images (+ alignments / CTF) to be analyzed. NOTE: If the metadata includes the label subtomo_labels, then TomoSIREN network will be trained (i.e., HetSIREN for tomography data). In this case, the parameter decoupling will not have any effect as pose/CTF decoupling is already handled by TomoSIREN.

fields.name: vol
fields.help: If provided, the neural network will learn how to refine this volume towards the heterogeneous states present in the images

fields.name: mask
fields.help: HetSIREN reconstruction mask (useful to focus the reconstruction/estimated landscape on a specific region of interest - the mask provided must be binary -  NOTE: since this is a reconstruction mask, it should be defined such that it covers the volume were the motions of interest are expected to happen)

fields.name: load_images_to_ram
fields.help: If provided, images will be loaded to RAM. This is recommended if you want the best performance and your dataset fits in your RAM memory. If this flag is not provided, images will be memory mapped. When this happens, the program will trade disk space for performance. Thus, during the execution additional disk space will be used and the performance will be slightly lower compared to loading the images to RAM. Disk usage will be back to normal once the execution has finished.

fields.name: sr
fields.help: Sampling rate of the images/volume

fields.name: lat_dim
fields.help: Dimensionality of the latent space of the network (set by default to 8)

fields.name: transport_mass
fields.help: When set, HetSIREN will be able to "move" the mass inside the mask instead of just reconstructing the volume. This implies that HetSIREN will estimate the motion to be applied to the points within the provided mask, instead of considering them fixed in space. This approach is useful when working with large box sizes that do not fit in GPU memory, or when a more through analysis of motions is desired. NOTE: When this option is set and a reference volume is provided, we recommend changing the reference mask to a tight mask computed from the reference volume. This mask now tells the program which regions should be moved. Therefore, consider providing a mask that covers all the protein regions you would like to be analyzed by HetSIREN.

fields.name: num_gaussians
fields.help: Before training the network, HetSIREN will try to fit a set of Gaussians in the reference volume to recreate it. The default criterium is to automatically determine the number of Gaussians neede to reproduce the reference volume with high-fidelity. However, if you prefer to fix the number of Gaussians in advance based on your own criterium (e.g., the number of residues in your protein), you can set this parameter. When set, the HetSIREN will fit this fixed number of Gaussians so that the reproduce the reference volume as well as possible.

fields.name: local_reconstruction
fields.help: When set, HetSIREN will turn to local heterogeneous reconstruction/refinement mod, focusing the analysis of heterogeneity to a region of interest enclosed by the provided refernece mask. WARNING: IF PROVIDED, TRANSPORT MASS WILL BE OVERRIDDEN AND NOT CONSIDERED. WARNING: IF PROVIDED, HAVING A REFERENCE VOLUME IS MANDATORY. OTHERWISE, THIS PARAMETER WILL BE NEGLECTED.

fields.name: ctf_type
fields.help: Determines whether to consider the CTF and, in case it is considered, whether it will be applied to the projections (apply) or used to correct the metadata images (wiener - precorrect)

fields.name: mode
fields.help:
train: train a neural network from scratch or from a previous execution if reload is provided
predict: predict the latent vectors from the input images (reload parameter is mandatory in this case)

fields.name: epochs
fields.help: Number of epochs to train the network (i.e. how many times to loop over the whole dataset of images - set to default to 50 - as a rule of thumb, consider 50 to 100 epochs enough for 100k images / if your dataset is bigger or smaller, scale this value proportionally to it

fields.name: batch_size
fields.help: Determines how many images will be load in the GPU at any moment during training (set by default to 8 - you can control GPU memory usage easily by tuning this parameter to fit your hardware requirements - we recommend using tools like nvidia-smi to monitor and/or measure memory usage and adjust this value - keep also in mind that bigger batch sizes might be less precise when looking for very local motions

fields.name: learning_rate
fields.help: The learning rate (lr) sets the speed of learning. Think of the model as trying to find the lowest point in a valley; the lr is the size of the step it takes on each attempt. A large lr (e.g., 0.01) is like taking huge leaps — it's fast but can be unstable, overshoot the lowest point, or cause NAN errors. A small lr (e.g., 1e-6) is like taking tiny shuffles — it's stable but very slow and might get stuck before reaching the bottom. A good default is often 0.0001. If training fails or errors explode, try making the lr 10 times smaller (e.g., 0.001 --> 0.0001).

fields.name: dataset_split_fraction
fields.help: Here you can provide the fractions to split your data automatically into a training and a validation subset following the format: training_fraction,validation_fraction. While the training subset will be used to train/update the network parameters, the validation subset will only be used to evaluate the accuracy of the network when faced with new data. Therefore, the validation subset will never be used to update the networks parameters. NOTE: the sum of training_fraction and validation_fraction must be equal to one.

fields.name: output_path
fields.help: Path to save the results (trained neural network, new metadata...)

fields.name: reload
fields.help: Path to a folder containing an already saved neural network (useful to fine tune a previous network - predict from new data - NOTE: If a reference volume was provided, HetSIREN also learns a gray level adjustment. In this case, reload must be the path to a folder containing two additional folders called: HetSIREN and Gaussian_volume_fitting)

fields.name: denoising_strength
fields.help: Determines how strongly HetSIREN will learn to remove noise from the resulting volumes. Increasing the value of this parameter will result in a stronger regularization of the noise, but it may affect the protein signal as well. (NOTE: We recommend setting this parameter in the range 0.0001 to 0.1)

fields.name: implicit_network
fields.help: When set, HetSIREN will use an implicit neural network approach to recover conformational states. Implicit neural networks are more memory consuming, but they are also more accurate in the detection of very local motions. If this architecture is selected, we strongly recommend to set as well the parameter total_mass to limit the memory consumption of the network and increase its performance.

fields.name: pose_refine_reg
fields.help: Strength of the geodesic anchor that keeps the per-image rigid pose refinement close to the input poses (penalizes 1 - cos(theta) of the refinement rotation). Larger values keep the refinement smaller/more conservative; set to 0 to disable it. (NOTE: this is the only regularizer acting on the rigid pose refinement in the default M=1 sampling regime)

fields.name: pose_refine_warmup_epochs
fields.help: Number of initial epochs over which the rigid pose refinement is ramped in from the identity. During this warmup the input poses are kept (almost) untouched so the conformation latent and decoder can settle before poses start being refined. Set to 0 to refine from the first step.

fields.name: train_inverse
fields.help: When set, HetSIREN will additionally train an inverse decoder that maps the output Gaussian positions (the deformed point cloud produced by the decoder) back to latent vectors. This provides a direct point-cloud -> latent encoding that complements the image-based encoder. NOTE: this is only meaningful when mass transport is enabled (--transport_mass), since the Gaussian positions only move in that mode; if set without mass transport it is ignored.

fields.name: point_transformer
fields.help: When set, HetSIREN will use a point transformer architecture in the decoder (operating directly on the Gaussian point cloud) instead of the default decoder. NOTE: this option and --implicit_network are mutually exclusive; if both are provided, the implicit network takes precedence and this flag is ignored. Like the implicit network, it only takes effect with mass transport (--transport_mass).

fields.name: decoupling_lambda
fields.help: Weight of the decoupling regularization (encourages the latent/conformation representation to be invariant to pose and CTF). Increase it to enforce stronger pose/CTF decoupling, decrease it (or set to 0) to relax it.

fields.name: distance_preservation_lambda
fields.help: Weight of the local distance preservation regularization (penalizes deviations of the mass-weighted point positions from the consensus/mean state, keeping local distances consistent). Increase it for stiffer, more locally rigid deformations, decrease it (or set to 0) for more flexibility.

fields.name: ssd_scratch_folder
fields.help: When the parameter load_images_to_ram is not provided, we strongly recommend to provide here a path to a folder in a SSD disk to read faster the data. If not given, the data will be loaded from the default disk.

fields.name: config
fields.help: Path to a YAML/JSON file with parameter values (keys are the argument names without the leading '--'). Values from the file act as defaults; any argument also given on the command line overrides them. NOTE: the fully-resolved parameters (file + command line) are written to <output_path>/run_config.json on every run, and that file can be reused as a --config to reproduce the run.

fields.name: vol

fields.name: mask

fields.name: load_images_to_ram
fields.help: If provided, images will be loaded to RAM. This is recommended if you want the best performance and your dataset fits in your RAM memory. fields.name: L1

fields.name: L2

If training fails or errors explode, try making the lr 10 times smaller (e.g., 0.001 --> 0.0001).

fields.name: dataset_split_fraction

fields.name: output_path
fields.help: Path to save the results (trained neural network, new metadata...)

fields.name: reload
fields.help: Path to a folder containing an already saved neural network (useful to fine tune a previous network - predict from new data - NOTE: Since Zernike3Deep also learns a gray level adjustment, reload must be the path to a folder containing two additional folders called: Zernike3Deep and Gaussian_volume_fitting)

fields.name: ssd_scratch_folder
fields.help: When the parameter load_images_to_ram is not provided, we strongly recommend to provide here a path to a folder in a SSD disk to read faster the data. If not given, the data will be loaded from the default disk.

fields.name: config
fields.help: Path to a YAML/JSON file with parameter values (keys are the argument names without the leading '--'). Values from the file act as defaults; any argument also given on the command line overrides them. NOTE: the fully-resolved parameters (file + command line) are written to <output_path>/run_config.json on every run, and that file can be reused as a --config to reproduce the run.

fields.name: input_space
fields.help: Paths to a series of .npy files containing the input spaces to be consensuated. NOTE: You can pass multiple times this parameter to specify a different file.NOTE: You can pass either the files directly or with the format "--input_space NAME:path" Using this alternative format allows giving identifiers to each input so it is easier to predict with the network later on. If only the file is given, each input will be named as "Input_#" based on their command line order.NOTE: If mode parameter is set to predict, we recommend using the NAME:path convention to simplify the prediction process. If not given, the network will attempt to indentify automatically your method.WARNING: The spaces stored in the files MUST have the SAME number of elements and they MUST be ordered (i.e. the first element in the files is the latent vector obtained from the first image and so on).

fields.name: lat_dim

fields.name: deconvolution_strength

fields.name: thr

fields.name: n_neighbours

fields.name: return_ids

fields.name: logdir
fields.help: Path to the TensorBoard log directory

annotate_space.name: annotate_space
annotate_space.description: Interactive latent space analysis with real time map generation

fields.name: z_space
fields.help: The latent space estimated by any method and saved in txt or npy format.

fields.name: z_space_reduced
fields.help: A reduced dimensionality version of your input latent space. If not provided, the viewer will use the original latent space provided through z_space will be displayed. Valid extensions include .txt and .npy

fields.name: path
fields.help: Path were viewer outputs will be saved.

fields.name: only_view
fields.help: When provided, the viewer will only display the conformational landscape. State generation capabilities are stopped. When neither env_name nor volumes_path are provided, the viewer will always use this mode.

fields.name: chimerax_binary
fields.help: If you want the viewer to connect with ChimeraX, please, provide here the absolute path to the ChimeraX binary from your installation.

fields.name: env_name
fields.help: When generating conformational states with a given software, you will need to provide here the name of the Conda environment where that software is installed

fields.name: server_functions_path
fields.help: When parameter env_name is provided, you must provide as well this parameter. Here, you must specify a path to a Python .py file containing a class with two methods: prepare_heterogeneity_program and decode_state_from_latent. These funcitons allows to setup and execute the heterogeneity method used to estimate the landscape provided through z_space, so that the viewer can generate conformations directly from this method. An example on how this class must be defined ca be found in this package source code available at: hax/viewers/server_loading_functions/load_model.py.

fields.name: volumes_path
fields.help: If env_name is not provided, you can still visualize a set of pre-saved conformation using this parameter. Here you will pass a path to a .txt file containing as many volume paths as points has the landscape provided in z_space. NOTE that the points in your landscape and the volume paths stored in the txt file MUST have the same order.

reconsiren.name: reconsiren
reconsiren.description: Ab initio estimation of particle pose, shifts and initial volume with neural networks

fields.name: md
fields.help: Xmipp/Relion metadata file with the images (+ alignments / CTF) to be analyzed

fields.name: vol
fields.help: If provided, the neural network will start from this volume when assigning the angles and shifts to the images.

fields.name: mask
fields.help: ReconSIREN reconstruction mask (the mask provided must be binary - NOTE: since this is a reconstruction mask, it should be defined such that it covers the volume were the motions of interest are expected to happen)

fields.name: num_gaussians
fields.help: Before training the network, HetSIREN will try to fit a set of Gaussians in the reference volume to recreate it. The default criterium is to automatically determine the number of Gaussians neede to reproduce the reference volume with high-fidelity. However, if you prefer to fix the number of Gaussians in advance based on your own criterium (e.g., the number of residues in your protein), you can set this parameter. When set, the HetSIREN will fit this fixed number of Gaussians so that the reproduce the reference volume as well as possible.

fields.name: load_images_to_ram
fields.help: If provided, images will be loaded to RAM. This is recommended if you want the best performance and your dataset fits in your RAM memory. If this flag is not provided, images will be memory mapped. When this happens, the program will trade disk space for performance. Thus, during the execution additional disk space will be used and the performance will be slightly lower compared to loading the images to RAM. Disk usage will be back to normal once the execution has finished.

fields.name: sr
fields.help: Sampling rate of the images/volume

fields.name: do_not_learn_volume
fields.help: When this parameter is provided, ReconSIREN will just learn an angular assignment with shifts without learning any map. This is usually useful when a reference volume with high resolution is provided (e.g. coming from an atomic model) and no refinement of the map is needed.

fields.name: refine_current_assignment
fields.help: If your input metadata has already and angular assignment and shifts, you can provide this option to refine those angles instead of finding an ab initio alignment.

fields.name: symmetry_group
fields.help: If your protein has any kind of symmetry, you may pass it here so that it is considered while learning the angular assignment and the volume (NOTE: only c* and d* symmetry groups are currently supported - the parameter is lower case sensitive - even if symmetry is provided, the network will learn a symmetry broken set of angles in c1. Therefore, the angles can be directly used in a reconstruction/refinement.)

fields.name: ctf_type
fields.help: Determines whether to consider the CTF and, in case it is considered, whether it will be applied to the projections (apply) or used to correct the metadata images (wiener - precorrect)

fields.name: mode
fields.help:
train: train a neural network from scratch or from a previous execution if reload is provided
predict: predict the latent vectors from the input images (reload parameter is mandatory in this case)

fields.name: epochs
fields.help: Number of epochs to train the network (i.e. how many times to loop over the whole dataset of images - set to default to 50 - as a rule of thumb, consider 50 to 100 epochs enough for 100k images / if your dataset is bigger or smaller, scale this value proportionally to it

fields.name: batch_size
fields.help: Determines how many images will be load in the GPU at any moment during training (set by default to 8 - you can control GPU memory usage easily by tuning this parameter to fit your hardware requirements - we recommend using tools like nvidia-smi to monitor and/or measure memory usage and adjust this value - keep also in mind that bigger batch sizes might be less precise when looking for very local motions

fields.name: learning_rate
fields.help: The learning rate (lr) sets the speed of learning. Think of the model as trying to find the lowest point in a valley; the lr is the size of the step it takes on each attempt. A large lr (e.g., 0.01) is like taking huge leaps — it's fast but can be unstable, overshoot the lowest point, or cause NAN errors. A small lr (e.g., 1e-6) is like taking tiny shuffles — it's stable but very slow and might get stuck before reaching the bottom. A good default is often 0.0001. If training fails or errors explode, try making the lr 10 times smaller (e.g., 0.001 --> 0.0001).

fields.name: dataset_split_fraction
fields.help: Here you can provide the fractions to split your data automatically into a training and a validation subset following the format: training_fraction,validation_fraction. While the training subset will be used to train/update the network parameters, the validation subset will only be used to evaluate the accuracy of the network when faced with new data. Therefore, the validation subset will never be used to update the networks parameters. NOTE: the sum of training_fraction and validation_fraction must be equal to one.

fields.name: output_path
fields.help: Path to save the results (trained neural network, new metadata...)

fields.name: reload
fields.help: Path to a folder containing an already saved neural network (useful to fine tune a previous network - predict from new data).
